travelAdvisory.summary:
Updated to reflect a shift to Level 2 “Exercise increased caution” for Mainland China.
Summary: Exercise increased caution when traveling to Mainland China due to arbitrary enforcement of local laws, including in relation to exit bans.
Exercise increased caution when traveling to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) due to the arbitrary enforcement of local laws.
Reconsider travel to the Macau Special Administrative Region (SAR) due to a limited ability to provide emergency consular

connectivity.simOptions: Foreign SIM cards and eSIMs work for calls/data but cannot access Google, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp without VPN. China Unicom or China Mobile tourist SIMs at airports.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at hotels, cafes, and airports but often requires Chinese phone number for registration. Many Western services are blocked.
connectivity.bestOption: Get a VPN before arriving (download in advance — VPN apps blocked in China). eSIM with roaming from Airalo or Holafly bypasses the firewall via foreign routing.

cultural.tipping: Not expected and not customary. Some high-end international hotels may accept tips. Taxi drivers do not expect tips.
cultural.dressCode: Modest dress at temples and religious sites. Cover shoulders and knees. Business settings are formal. Casual dress is fine in cities.
cultural.greetings: Handshake is common in business. Slight nod for casual greetings. Address people by title + surname. Business cards exchanged with both hands.
taboos: Sticking chopsticks upright in rice (funeral symbolism)
Writing names in red ink (associated with death)
Giving clocks as gifts (sounds like 'attending a funeral')
Discussing Taiwan, Tibet, or Tiananmen Square politics
cultural.haggling: Expected at markets, street vendors, and some small shops. Not at department stores, malls, or restaurants. Start at 30-50% of asking price.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: visa required. Transit visa-free for 144h in select cities. Most Western nationals need a visa.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: March-May (spring) and September-November (autumn). Avoid Chinese New Year (late Jan/Feb) and Golden Week (Oct 1-7) — extreme crowds.
